text:
[
  {"n": 1, "kind": "Example", "title": "Empirical Probability of Coin Tosses", "source": "Lecture 1", "statement": "A coin is tossed 1000 times and lands on Heads 510 times. Calculate the empirical probability of getting Heads."},
  {"n": 2, "kind": "Example", "title": "Die Toss Sample Spaces with Varying Granularity", "source": "Lecture 1", "statement": "Consider the experiment of tossing a die. Specify the sample space when observing the exact upward face versus observing only whether the number is even or odd."},
  {"n": 3, "kind": "Example", "title": "Electronic Component Lifetime Event", "source": "Lecture 1", "statement": "Given the sample space S = {t | t >= 0} representing the lifetime in years of an electronic component, describe the event that the component fails before the end of the fifth year."},
  {"n": 4, "kind": "Example", "title": "Intersection of Student Attributes", "source": "Lecture 1", "statement": "Let E be the event that a student chosen at random is an engineering major, and let F be the event that the student is female. Identify the event E ∩ F."},
  {"n": 5, "kind": "Example", "title": "Complement of an Item Set", "source": "Lecture 1", "statement": "Given the sample space S = {book, cell phone, mp3, paper, stationery, laptop} and the event A = {book, stationery, laptop, paper}, determine the complement of A."},
  {"n": 6, "kind": "Example", "title": "Mutually Exclusive Television Channels", "source": "Lecture 1", "statement": "A cable television company offers eight channels, including NBC and CBS affiliates. Determine whether selecting an NBC channel and selecting a CBS channel at random are mutually exclusive events."},
  {"n": 7, "kind": "Example", "title": "Union of Discrete Sets", "source": "Lecture 1", "statement": "Find the union of sets A = {a, b, c} and B = {b, c, d, e}."},
  {"n": 8, "kind": "Example", "title": "Union of Behavioral Events and Real Intervals", "source": "Lecture 1", "statement": "Express the event that a randomly selected employee either drinks or smokes or does both. Also, determine the union of the real intervals M = (3, 9) and N = (5, 12)."},
  {"n": 9, "kind": "Example", "title": "Probability of at Least One Head in Two Tosses", "source": "Lecture 1", "statement": "A fair coin is tossed twice. Find the probability that at least one head occurs."},
  {"n": 10, "kind": "Example", "title": "Probability on a Loaded Die", "source": "Lecture 1", "statement": "A die is weighted so that an even outcome is twice as likely as an odd outcome. Find the probability of rolling a number strictly less than 4."},
  {"n": 11, "kind": "Example", "title": "Union and Intersection on a Loaded Die", "source": "Lecture 1", "statement": "For a loaded die where even numbers have twice the probability of odd numbers, let A be the event of rolling an even number and B be the event of rolling a number divisible by 3. Find P(A ∪ B) and P(A ∩ B)."},
  {"n": 12, "kind": "Example", "title": "Engineering Major Selection Probabilities", "source": "Lecture 1", "statement": "A class consists of 25 industrial, 10 mechanical, 10 electrical, and 8 civil engineering students. Find the probability that a randomly chosen student is (a) an industrial engineering major and (b) a civil or electrical engineering major."},
  {"n": 13, "kind": "Example", "title": "Job Offer Probabilities from Two Companies", "source": "Lecture 1", "statement": "A graduating student has a 0.8 probability of receiving an offer from company A, a 0.6 probability from company B, and a 0.5 probability from both. Find the probability of receiving at least one offer."},
  {"n": 14, "kind": "Example", "title": "Sum of Seven or Eleven on Two Dice", "source": "Lecture 1", "statement": "Find the probability of rolling a total sum of 7 or 11 when a pair of fair six-sided dice is tossed."},
  {"n": 15, "kind": "Example", "title": "Complement Rule for Mechanic Service Volume", "source": "Lecture 1", "statement": "An automobile mechanic services 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, or 8 or more cars on a given day with probabilities 0.12, 0.19, 0.28, 0.24, 0.10, and 0.07, respectively. Find the probability that he services at least 5 cars on his next workday."},
  {"n": 16, "kind": "Example", "title": "Single Outcome on a Fair Die", "source": "Lecture 1", "statement": "Calculate the probability of rolling a 4 on a fair six-sided die."},
  {"n": 17, "kind": "Example", "title": "Meeting Probability of Two Friends", "source": "Lecture 1", "statement": "Two friends arrive independently and uniformly at random between 12:00 and 13:00 at a meeting point and wait for 15 minutes. Find the probability that they successfully meet."},
  {"n": 18, "kind": "Task", "title": "Three Coin Tosses and Event Formulations", "source": "Tutorial 2", "statement": "A coin is tossed three times. Write down the sample space S, express events A (exactly two heads), B (at least one head), and C (first toss is a head) as subsets, find their probabilities and intersections, and verify the addition rule."},
  {"n": 19, "kind": "Task", "title": "Server Cluster Reliability and De Morgan's Law", "source": "Tutorial 2", "statement": "A cluster consists of three servers where A_i denotes the event that server i is up. Express various cluster operational events in terms of A_i, and prove De Morgan's law for three events."},
  {"n": 20, "kind": "Task", "title": "Examination Passing Probabilities and Partitions", "source": "Tutorial 2", "statement": "A student takes exams in Calculus and Linear Algebra with passing probabilities 0.7 and 0.6, respectively, and joint passing probability 0.5. Find the probability of passing at least one exam, neither exam, exactly one exam, and Calculus but not Linear Algebra."},
  {"n": 21, "kind": "Task", "title": "Three-Event Inclusion-Exclusion and Overlaps", "source": "Tutorial 2", "statement": "Given three events A, B, and C with specified marginal, pairwise, and triple intersection probabilities, find the probability that at least one, none, at least two, or exactly one of the events occurs."},
  {"n": 22, "kind": "Task", "title": "Probability Identities and Set Differences", "source": "Tutorial 2", "statement": "Given P(A) = 0.4, P(B) = 0.5, and P(A ∪ B) = 0.7, compute P(A ∩ B), P(A^c ∩ B^c), P(A \\ B), P(A^c ∪ B^c), and the symmetric difference probability."},
  {"n": 23, "kind": "Task", "title": "Defective Item Sampling Without Replacement", "source": "Tutorial 2", "statement": "Four items are drawn at random without replacement from a batch of 10 items containing 3 defectives. Find the probability that the selection contains no defectives, exactly one defective, and at least one defective."},
  {"n": 24, "kind": "Task", "title": "Meeting Time Interval and Waiting Optimization", "source": "Tutorial 2", "statement": "Two people arrive uniformly and independently between 12:00 and 13:00, each waiting 15 minutes. Find the probability that they meet, and determine the waiting duration needed for the probability of meeting to reach at least 1/2."},
  {"n": 25, "kind": "Task", "title": "Broken Stick Triangle Formation", "source": "Tutorial 2", "statement": "A stick of length 1 is broken at two points chosen independently and uniformly on [0, 1]. Find the probability that the three resulting segments can form a triangle."},
  {"n": 26, "kind": "Task", "title": "Axiom Verification on Finite Sets", "source": "Tutorial 2", "statement": "Given a four-element sample space, determine which of four specified set functions define valid probability measures and identify which axioms fail for the invalid functions."},
  {"n": 27, "kind": "Task", "title": "Probability Measures on Countable Sample Spaces", "source": "Tutorial 2", "statement": "On the positive integers, find the constant c such that P({k}) = c / 3^k is a probability measure and compute related event probabilities. Determine whether assigning 0 to finite sets and 1 to infinite sets defines a valid probability measure."},
  {"n": 28, "kind": "Task", "title": "Identification and Generation of Sigma-Algebras", "source": "Tutorial 2", "statement": "For a four-element set, determine which given collections of subsets are sigma-algebras and identify failing properties. Then construct the smallest sigma-algebra generated by two singletons."},
  {"n": 29, "kind": "Task", "title": "Axiomatic Proofs and Sigma-Algebra Closures", "source": "Tutorial 2", "statement": "Prove from Kolmogorov's axioms that P(∅) = 0 and that probability is monotonic. Prove that the intersection of two sigma-algebras is a sigma-algebra, and show by counterexample that their union is not necessarily one."}
]
